sections.heading: C — Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles
sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road with vulnerable users and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A95
Use courtesy, respect for others' rights and heightened awareness when different road users share a roadway. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A95
When an approaching police or emergency vehicle uses a siren or flashing red or blue lights, promptly pull to the right-side curb or road edge, stop and stay stopped until it passes ahead. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A95
When approaching a stopped flashing-light police or emergency vehicle, or a tow or incident-response vehicle, immediately slow below the posted limit and proceed cautiously. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A95
For the stopped-vehicle response on a road with at least two lanes in the same direction, move to a nonadjacent lane as soon as safely possible. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A95
Watch for pedestrians around homes, schools and crossings, trails, parking areas, intersections, bus stops, playgrounds and parks. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A96
Yield to a pedestrian in either a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A96
A driver entering a street from an alley or driveway must yield to pedestrians. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A96
Yield to a pedestrian with a clearly visible white cane or an accompanying service dog. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A96
A pedestrian crossing away from both a crosswalk and an intersection must yield to motor vehicles. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A96
Pedestrians must yield when an intersection or crosswalk signal directs them to do so. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A96
Stop for a pedestrian already crossing without a painted crosswalk and allow the crossing to finish, even when the driver technically has priority. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A96
If a pedestrian enters the crosswalk just before a red signal becomes green, wait for the pedestrian to cross before proceeding. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A96
At an intersection with two lanes in the same direction, do not pass a vehicle stopped in the right lane for a pedestrian; wait for the crossing and check safety before proceeding. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A97
Use extreme care for pedestrians at night or when rain, snow, fog or sun glare reduces visibility. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A97
In places children may be near the road, take extra care and walk around the vehicle before entry to check for children hidden from the driver's seat. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A97
When reversing from a driveway, watch for children who might run behind the vehicle. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A97
Use extra care around roadside parked cars and visible children because another child may be hidden nearby. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A97
Horseback riders may use most public roads and have the same road rights and rule obligations as motor-vehicle drivers. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A97
When approaching a mounted rider, slow down and avoid frightening the horse. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A98
Do not sound a horn near a horse because startling it can cause a crash. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A98
If a rider is struggling to control an animal, use extreme care when going around and stop if needed to avoid joining the hazard. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A98
Bicyclists have driver-like road rights and must travel with traffic flow. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A98
A bicyclist rides as close to the right edge as safety allows except while passing, turning left, avoiding obstacles or where safe side-by-side travel is impossible. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A98
When passing a cyclist, move left if possible; otherwise leave as much clearance as possible, with at least three feet as a safe margin, waiting for opposing traffic to clear if needed. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A98
Slow when passing children on bicycles and expect unpredictable movement toward the lane. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A98
At an Idaho stop sign, a bicyclist need not fully stop but must yield to vehicles in or already at the intersection, or close enough to be hazardous, and then proceed cautiously. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A99
A bicyclist turning right on red need not fully stop, but must yield to vehicles in the intersection or close enough to present a hazard. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A99
Before a right turn from a stop, check right first and also look left and behind for a cyclist approaching or standing alongside. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A99
If a cyclist is ahead before a right turn, slow and remain behind until the cyclist has passed the intended turn point. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A99
A right turn across a cyclist's path can cause the broadside conflict called a right hook. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A99
A right turn on a street with a bicycle lane crosses a dedicated travel lane, so actively look for cyclists. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A99
When going through or turning at an intersection, scan its corners more than once. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A100
Dashed bicycle-lane lines permit an expected merge; check for cyclists first, and use the dashed area when preparing the described intersection right turn. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A100
The handbook says bicycle use of sidewalks is permitted in most communities and is not compulsory. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A100
Use extreme caution entering or leaving a driveway because young children may cycle on the sidewalk. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A100
Pass child cyclists with extra room and caution because they may change direction unexpectedly. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A100
Do not hurry a turn or squeeze past a cyclist merely to beat traffic or a signal. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A100
On a narrow stretch where passing is unsafe, a cyclist may need the lane center; do not follow too closely. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A100
Expect and deliberately look for cyclists because their size, road position and speed can make them less noticeable. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0100]

Misconceptions: A motorcycle is entitled to its full lane, a truck's right-turn setup can extend left and a cyclist may need the center of a narrow lane. A flashing motorcycle indicator alone does not prove a turn.
Mnemonic: See, leave space and wait is a teaching cue for the supported road-sharing decisions.
Glossary: A right hook is a turning conflict across a cyclist's path; a sharrow marks a preferred shared-lane cycling position; a pilot vehicle warns of an unusually large load.
Dynamic facts: present traffic, visibility, local cycling controls and applicable vehicle restrictions determine actual road-sharing decisions.

verification_debt.claim_text: The children-near-roadway instruction on physical page ninety-six continues onto ninety-seven with its unexpected-entry qualifier. Nearby complete child-safety instructions are covered; this complete cross-page instruction remains unresolved under the one-page fact binding.

The horse-passing instruction spans physical pages ninety-seven and ninety-eight. Approaching-rider slowing, no horn and control-difficulty response have local support, but the complete passing-room instruction needs a supported multi-page fact binding.

The bicycle straight-through red-light permission on physical page ninety-eight continues onto ninety-nine to complete the close-enough-to-be-a-hazard qualifier. That complete exception is withheld as coverage debt rather than truncating its yielding condition.

The repeated intersection-look discussion spans physical pages ninety-nine and one hundred. The local repeated-scan instruction is covered; the full closing rationale and numeric travel-distance example are not represented as a complete one-page fact.

The passing-distance paragraph starts on physical page one hundred and continues onto one hundred one with the pavement-edge distance and emergency-space explanation. The complete paragraph requires a multi-page binding; the independently complete motorist passing-clearance rules on one hundred one are covered.

Physical page ninety-eight says bicycles are allowed on all Idaho roadways without enumerating access restrictions or posted exceptions. Rights, direction and lane-position guidance are covered; the universal access assertion is withheld pending exact official exception evidence.
